# Load Libraries
```{julia}
#| output: false
using Pumas
using Random
using Distributions
using LinearAlgebra
using Statistics
using DataFrames
using Bioequivalence
using CairoMakie
using Makie
using Logging
```

# Set Random Seed
```{julia}
#| output: false
Random.seed!(142)
```

# PK Model

Same model as the parallel and crossover versions. `tvbio` controls relative
bioavailability of Test vs Reference via `@dosecontrol`.

```{julia}
#| output: false
pkmodel = @model begin
    @param begin
        tvcl  ∈ RealDomain(lower=0)
        tvv   ∈ RealDomain(lower=0)
        tvka  ∈ RealDomain(lower=0)
        tvbio ∈ RealDomain(lower=0)
        Ω     ∈ PDiagDomain(3)
        σ     ∈ RealDomain(lower=0)
    end

    @random begin
        η ~ MvNormal(Ω)
    end

    @covariates TRT

    @pre begin
        CL  = tvcl * exp(η[1])
        V   = tvv  * exp(η[2])
        Ka  = tvka * exp(η[3])
    end

    @dosecontrol begin
        bioav = (Depot = TRT == "T" ? tvbio : 1.0,)
    end

    @dynamics begin
        Depot'   = -Ka * Depot
        Central' =  Ka * Depot - (CL / V) * Central
    end

    @derived begin
        cp = @. Central / V
        dv ~ @. Normal(cp, σ)
    end
end
```

# True Parameter Values
```{julia}
#| output: false
θ_true = (
    tvcl  = 5.0,
    tvv   = 50.0,
    tvka  = 1.2,
    tvbio = 1.0,
    Ω     = Diagonal([0.5, 0.5, 0.3]),   # ~30% CV IIV
    σ     = 0.2
)
```

# Partial Replicate Simulation Helpers

## Design rationale

In a **3-period partial replicate design** (TRR/RTR), each subject receives the
Test formulation once and the Reference formulation twice, in one of two randomized
sequences:

| Sequence | Period 1 | Period 2 | Period 3 |
|----------|----------|----------|----------|
| 1        | T        | R        | R        |
| 2        | R        | T        | R        |

**Key advantages over a standard 2x2 crossover:**

- **Within-reference variability estimation:** Two Reference periods per subject
  allow direct estimation of within-subject variability for Reference (σ²_WR).
- **Reference-Scaled Average BE (RSABE):** For highly variable drugs (CV_WR > 30%),
  regulatory guidelines (FDA, EMA) allow widened BE limits scaled to σ_WR,
  dramatically improving power while controlling type I error.
- **Regulatory acceptance:** FDA explicitly recommends partial replicate designs
  for HVD bioequivalence studies.

The simulation ensures the same η is used across all three periods for each subject
by sampling η once and baking it into individual typical values.

```{julia}
#| output: false
"""Create parallel-design population (used only for parameter estimation)."""
function create_be_population(n_per_arm)
    subjects = Subject[]
    for trt in ["R", "T"], i in 1:n_per_arm
        push!(subjects, Subject(
            id     = length(subjects) + 1,
            events = DosageRegimen(100, time = 0),
            covariates = (TRT = trt,)
        ))
    end
    return Population(subjects)
end

"""Simulate a parallel BE trial (used only for parameter estimation)."""
function simulate_be_trial(params; n_per_arm = 30)
    pop = create_be_population(n_per_arm)
    return simobs(pkmodel, pop, params; obstimes = 0:1:72)
end

"""
Simulate a 3-period partial replicate BE trial (TRR / RTR).

Each of `n_subjects` subjects receives Reference twice and Test once,
with the **same individual eta** across all three periods.

Returns a NamedTuple with :T, :R1, :R2 (vectors of per-subject sims)
and :n_subjects.
"""
function simulate_partial_replicate_trial(params; n_subjects = 30)
    # Sample between-subject random effects once per subject
    ηs = [rand(MvNormal(zeros(3), params.Ω)) for _ in 1:n_subjects]
    tiny_Ω = Diagonal(fill(1e-8, 3))   # near-zero — IIV already baked into typical values

    sims_T  = Vector{Any}(undef, n_subjects)
    sims_R1 = Vector{Any}(undef, n_subjects)
    sims_R2 = Vector{Any}(undef, n_subjects)

    for i in 1:n_subjects
        η = ηs[i]
        # Individual parameters: absorb η into typical values
        ind_p = (
            tvcl  = params.tvcl * exp(η[1]),
            tvv   = params.tvv  * exp(η[2]),
            tvka  = params.tvka * exp(η[3]),
            tvbio = params.tvbio,
            Ω     = tiny_Ω,
            σ     = params.σ
        )

        # Three periods per subject — unique IDs for NCA processing
        subj_T  = Subject(id = i,                  events = DosageRegimen(100, time=0), covariates = (TRT = "T",))
        subj_R1 = Subject(id = i + n_subjects,     events = DosageRegimen(100, time=0), covariates = (TRT = "R",))
        subj_R2 = Subject(id = i + 2*n_subjects,   events = DosageRegimen(100, time=0), covariates = (TRT = "R",))

        sims_T[i]  = simobs(pkmodel, subj_T,  ind_p; obstimes = 0:1:72)
        sims_R1[i] = simobs(pkmodel, subj_R1, ind_p; obstimes = 0:1:72)
        sims_R2[i] = simobs(pkmodel, subj_R2, ind_p; obstimes = 0:1:72)
    end

    return (T = sims_T, R1 = sims_R1, R2 = sims_R2, n_subjects = n_subjects)
end
```

# Simulate Reference Trial and Fit

Parameter estimation uses a parallel-design trial to obtain model parameter
estimates and their uncertainty. The study design for virtual BE trials
(partial replicate here) is independent of the design used for estimation.

```{julia}
#| output: false
ref_sim = simulate_be_trial(θ_true; n_per_arm = 30)

sim_pop = read_pumas(
    DataFrame(ref_sim);
    id = :id, time = :time, observations = [:dv],
    amt = :amt, evid = :evid, covariates = [:TRT], cmt = :cmt
)

init = (
    tvcl  = 4.5,
    tvv   = 45.0,
    tvka  = 1.0,
    tvbio = 1.0,
    Ω     = Diagonal([0.3, 0.4, 0.5]),
    σ     = 0.3
)

fit_res = fit(pkmodel, sim_pop, init, Pumas.FOCE())
θ̂ = coef(fit_res)
nothing
```

# Uncertainty Extraction

## Sampling helper
```{julia}
#| output: false
"""
Sample `n` parameter NamedTuples from a MvNormal on the estimation (log) scale.
"""
function sample_from_vcov(mean_params, V, n)
    μ = [
        log(mean_params.tvcl), log(mean_params.tvv),
        log(mean_params.tvka), log(mean_params.tvbio),
        log(mean_params.Ω[1,1]), log(mean_params.Ω[2,2]), log(mean_params.Ω[3,3]),
        log(mean_params.σ)
    ]
    dist = MvNormal(μ, Symmetric(V))
    return [begin
        s = rand(dist)
        (tvcl  = exp(s[1]), tvv  = exp(s[2]),
         tvka  = exp(s[3]), tvbio = exp(s[4]),
         Ω     = Diagonal([exp(s[5]), exp(s[6]), exp(s[7])]),
         σ     = exp(s[8]))
    end for _ in 1:n]
end
```

## Method 1: VCOV (Asymptotic Normal)
```{julia}
#| output: false
vcov_param_samples = sample_from_vcov(θ̂, vcov(fit_res), 200)
```

## Method 2: Bootstrap
```{julia}
#| output: false
boot_settings = Bootstrap(
    samples = 100,
    stratify_by = nothing,
    ensemblealg = EnsembleThreads()
)
boot_inf = infer(fit_res, boot_settings; level = 0.95)

boot_param_samples = sample_from_vcov(coef(boot_inf), vcov(boot_inf), 200)
nothing
```

## Method 3: SIR
```{julia}
#| output: false
sir_settings = SIR(samples = 200, resamples = 100)
sir_inf = infer(fit_res, sir_settings; level = 0.95)

sir_param_samples = sample_from_vcov(coef(sir_inf), vcov(sir_inf), 200)
nothing
```

# TOST for Partial Replicate BE

## Statistical methods

In a partial replicate design, two complementary BE approaches are available:

| Approach | When used | BE limits | Advantage |
|----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| **Unscaled (standard TOST)** | CV_WR ≤ 30% | Fixed 80–125% | Standard regulatory acceptance |
| **RSABE (reference-scaled)** | CV_WR > 30% | Scaled to σ_WR + GMR 80–125% | Much higher power for HVDs |

**Unscaled TOST** uses within-subject differences:
$d_i = \log(T_i) - \frac{\log(R_{1i}) + \log(R_{2i})}{2}$

**RSABE** additionally estimates within-reference variance from the paired R periods:
$\hat{\sigma}^2_{WR} = \frac{1}{2n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (\log R_{1i} - \log R_{2i})^2$

and applies the scaled criterion: $|\hat{\mu}_T - \hat{\mu}_R| \leq \theta_s \cdot \hat{\sigma}_{WR}$
where $\theta_s = \ln(1.25) / 0.25 \approx 0.893$, plus a point estimate constraint (0.80 ≤ GMR ≤ 1.25).

## NCA and analysis helpers

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| echo: false
"""Find first matching column from `candidates` in DataFrame `df`."""
function find_col(df, candidates)
    ns = names(df)
    for c in candidates
        string(c) in ns && return Symbol(c)
    end
    error("None of $candidates found in columns: $ns")
end

# Detect AUC and Cmax column names once from the reference NCA table
const AUC_COL  = find_col(nca_tbl_ref, ["aucinf_obs", "aucinf", "auclast", "AUC", "auc"])
const CMAX_COL = find_col(nca_tbl_ref, ["cmax", "Cmax", "CMAX"])

"""Convert a vector of individual simobs results to a sorted NCA report table."""
function sims_to_nca(sims)
    simdf = vcat([DataFrame(s) for s in sims]...)
    simdf.route .= "ev"
    simdf.dv .= max.(simdf.dv, 0.0)

    tbl = with_logger(NullLogger()) do
        ncapop = read_nca(simdf;
            id = :id, time = :time, amt = :amt,
            observations = :dv, route = :route
        )
        nca_out = run_nca(ncapop)
        nca_out.reportdf
    end
    return sort(tbl, :id)
end

"""Extract non-missing, positive values from a column as Float64 vector."""
function clean_pk_col(df, col)
    vals = df[!, col]
    return Float64[v for v in vals if !ismissing(v) && v > 0]
end

"""
Unscaled TOST for partial replicate design.
Uses within-subject differences: d_i = log(T_i) - mean(log(R1_i), log(R2_i)).
"""
function tost_partial_replicate(log_T, log_R1, log_R2; alpha = 0.05, θ_L = 0.80, θ_U = 1.25)
    n = length(log_T)
    n < 2 && return (gmr=NaN, ci_lo=NaN, ci_hi=NaN, pass=false)

    log_R_avg = (log_R1 .+ log_R2) ./ 2
    d  = log_T .- log_R_avg
    Δ  = mean(d)
    se = std(d) / sqrt(n)
    df = n - 1
    tc = quantile(TDist(df), 1 - alpha)

    gmr   = exp(Δ)
    ci_lo = exp(Δ - tc * se)
    ci_hi = exp(Δ + tc * se)
    pass  = ci_lo >= θ_L && ci_hi <= θ_U

    return (gmr=gmr, ci_lo=ci_lo, ci_hi=ci_hi, pass=pass)
end

"""
Reference-Scaled Average Bioequivalence (RSABE) for partial replicate design.

FDA approach:
- Estimates within-reference variance (σ²_WR) from paired R periods
- If CV_WR ≤ 30%: standard unscaled TOST (80–125%)
- If CV_WR > 30%: scaled criterion |μT − μR| ≤ θs × σ_WR, plus GMR constraint
  where θs = ln(1.25) / 0.25
"""
function rsabe_partial_replicate(log_T, log_R1, log_R2; alpha = 0.05)
    n = length(log_T)
    n < 2 && return (gmr=NaN, ci_lo=NaN, ci_hi=NaN, pass_unscaled=false, pass_rsabe=false, sWR=NaN, cvWR=NaN)

    # Within-subject difference: T vs average of two R periods
    log_R_avg = (log_R1 .+ log_R2) ./ 2
    d  = log_T .- log_R_avg
    Δ  = mean(d)
    se = std(d) / sqrt(n)
    df = n - 1
    tc = quantile(TDist(df), 1 - alpha)

    gmr   = exp(Δ)
    ci_lo = exp(Δ - tc * se)
    ci_hi = exp(Δ + tc * se)
    pass_unscaled = ci_lo >= 0.80 && ci_hi <= 1.25

    # Within-reference variance from paired R observations
    diff_R = log_R1 .- log_R2
    sWR²   = sum(diff_R .^ 2) / (2 * n)
    sWR    = sqrt(sWR²)
    cvWR   = 100 * sqrt(exp(sWR²) - 1)

    if cvWR ≤ 30.0
        # Low variability: standard unscaled TOST applies
        pass_rsabe = pass_unscaled
    else
        # High variability: reference-scaled criterion
        θs = log(1.25) / 0.25   # ≈ 0.893
        scaled_limit = θs * sWR
        pass_rsabe = abs(Δ) ≤ scaled_limit && gmr >= 0.80 && gmr <= 1.25
    end

    return (gmr=gmr, ci_lo=ci_lo, ci_hi=ci_hi, pass_unscaled=pass_unscaled,
            pass_rsabe=pass_rsabe, sWR=sWR, cvWR=cvWR)
end

"""
Run NCA on a partial replicate trial, then apply both unscaled TOST and RSABE.
Returns detailed results or `nothing` if insufficient paired data.
"""
function run_be_on_partial_replicate_detailed(trial)
    tbl_T  = sims_to_nca(trial.T)
    tbl_R1 = sims_to_nca(trial.R1)
    tbl_R2 = sims_to_nca(trial.R2)

    n_pairs = min(nrow(tbl_T), nrow(tbl_R1), nrow(tbl_R2))
    n_pairs < 2 && return nothing

    # Build paired log-vectors — drop triplets where any value is missing/non-positive
    auc_lT,  auc_lR1,  auc_lR2  = Float64[], Float64[], Float64[]
    cmax_lT, cmax_lR1, cmax_lR2 = Float64[], Float64[], Float64[]

    for i in 1:n_pairs
        at, ar1, ar2 = tbl_T[i, AUC_COL], tbl_R1[i, AUC_COL], tbl_R2[i, AUC_COL]
        ct, cr1, cr2 = tbl_T[i, CMAX_COL], tbl_R1[i, CMAX_COL], tbl_R2[i, CMAX_COL]

        if !any(ismissing, (at, ar1, ar2)) && all(>(0), (at, ar1, ar2))
            push!(auc_lT,  log(Float64(at)))
            push!(auc_lR1, log(Float64(ar1)))
            push!(auc_lR2, log(Float64(ar2)))
        end
        if !any(ismissing, (ct, cr1, cr2)) && all(>(0), (ct, cr1, cr2))
            push!(cmax_lT,  log(Float64(ct)))
            push!(cmax_lR1, log(Float64(cr1)))
            push!(cmax_lR2, log(Float64(cr2)))
        end
    end

    (length(auc_lT) < 2 || length(cmax_lT) < 2) && return nothing

    auc_res  = rsabe_partial_replicate(auc_lT,  auc_lR1,  auc_lR2)
    cmax_res = rsabe_partial_replicate(cmax_lT, cmax_lR1, cmax_lR2)

    return (
        auc_gmr      = auc_res.gmr,
        auc_lo       = auc_res.ci_lo,
        auc_hi       = auc_res.ci_hi,
        auc_pass     = auc_res.pass_rsabe,
        auc_pass_unscaled = auc_res.pass_unscaled,
        auc_cvWR     = auc_res.cvWR,
        cmax_gmr     = cmax_res.gmr,
        cmax_lo      = cmax_res.ci_lo,
        cmax_hi      = cmax_res.ci_hi,
        cmax_pass    = cmax_res.pass_rsabe,
        cmax_pass_unscaled = cmax_res.pass_unscaled,
        cmax_cvWR    = cmax_res.cvWR,
        overall_pass = auc_res.pass_rsabe && cmax_res.pass_rsabe,
        overall_pass_unscaled = auc_res.pass_unscaled && cmax_res.pass_unscaled
    )
end
```

# Within-Reference %CV Estimation Helper
```{julia}
#| output: false
#| echo: false
"""
Estimate within-reference (intra-subject) %CV for AUC and Cmax from simulated
partial replicate trials at T/R = 1.0.

Uses paired Reference observations: σ²_WR = Σ(log R1 - log R2)² / (2n).
%CV_WR = 100 × sqrt(exp(σ²_WR) - 1).
"""
function estimate_cv_within_ref(param_samples; n_subjects = 60, n_reps = 50)
    auc_wr_vars  = Float64[]
    cmax_wr_vars = Float64[]

    for _ in 1:n_reps
        θ_draw     = param_samples[rand(1:length(param_samples))]
        sim_params = merge(θ_draw, (tvbio = 1.0,))

        try
            trial  = simulate_partial_replicate_trial(sim_params; n_subjects = n_subjects)
            tbl_R1 = sims_to_nca(trial.R1)
            tbl_R2 = sims_to_nca(trial.R2)

            n_pairs = min(nrow(tbl_R1), nrow(tbl_R2))

            auc_diff  = Float64[]
            cmax_diff = Float64[]

            for i in 1:n_pairs
                ar1, ar2 = tbl_R1[i, AUC_COL], tbl_R2[i, AUC_COL]
                cr1, cr2 = tbl_R1[i, CMAX_COL], tbl_R2[i, CMAX_COL]

                if !any(ismissing, (ar1, ar2)) && ar1 > 0 && ar2 > 0
                    push!(auc_diff, log(Float64(ar1)) - log(Float64(ar2)))
                end
                if !any(ismissing, (cr1, cr2)) && cr1 > 0 && cr2 > 0
                    push!(cmax_diff, log(Float64(cr1)) - log(Float64(cr2)))
                end
            end

            # Within-reference variance: σ²_WR = Σ(diff²) / (2n)
            if length(auc_diff) >= 2
                push!(auc_wr_vars, sum(auc_diff .^ 2) / (2 * length(auc_diff)))
            end
            if length(cmax_diff) >= 2
                push!(cmax_wr_vars, sum(cmax_diff .^ 2) / (2 * length(cmax_diff)))
            end
        catch
            continue
        end
    end

    auc_cv  = 100 * sqrt(exp(mean(auc_wr_vars))  - 1)
    cmax_cv = 100 * sqrt(exp(mean(cmax_wr_vars)) - 1)
    return (auc_cv=auc_cv, cmax_cv=cmax_cv)
end
```

# Virtual BE Simulation Engine (Partial Replicate)
```{julia}
#| output: false
#| code-summary: "Virtual BE simulation engine — partial replicate design (click to expand)"
const SAMPLE_SIZES = [12, 24, 30, 40, 50, 60, 80]
const TR_RATIOS    = [0.7, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.3]

"""
Run virtual partial replicate BE simulations across all combinations of T/R ratios
and sample sizes.

**n_subjects** = total subjects per trial. Each subject receives T once and R twice
(3 periods total).

Tracks both RSABE (primary) and unscaled TOST pass rates.

Returns a NamedTuple with :summary and :detailed DataFrames.
"""
function virtual_be_sim(param_samples, method_name;
                        tr_ratios       = TR_RATIOS,
                        n_subjects_list = SAMPLE_SIZES,
                        n_sims          = 200)

    summary_results = DataFrame(
        method              = String[],
        tr_ratio            = Float64[],
        n_subjects          = Int[], 
        n_pass              = Int[],
        n_pass_unscaled     = Int[],
        n_valid             = Int[],
        n_error             = Int[],
        pass_rate           = Float64[],
        pass_rate_unscaled  = Float64[]
    )

    detailed_results = DataFrame(
        method       = String[],
        tr_ratio     = Float64[],
        n_subjects   = Int[],
        sim_id       = Int[],
        auc_gmr      = Float64[],
        auc_lo       = Float64[],
        auc_hi       = Float64[],
        auc_pass     = Bool[],
        cmax_gmr     = Float64[],
        cmax_lo      = Float64[],
        cmax_hi      = Float64[],
        cmax_pass    = Bool[],
        overall_pass = Bool[]
    )

    for n_subj in n_subjects_list, tr in tr_ratios
        n_pass  = 0
        n_pass_unscaled = 0
        n_error = 0

        for i in 1:n_sims
            θ_draw     = param_samples[rand(1:length(param_samples))]
            sim_params = merge(θ_draw, (tvbio = tr,))

            try
                trial = simulate_partial_replicate_trial(sim_params; n_subjects = n_subj)
                res   = run_be_on_partial_replicate_detailed(trial)

                if res === nothing
                    n_error += 1
                else
                    res.overall_pass && (n_pass += 1)
                    res.overall_pass_unscaled && (n_pass_unscaled += 1)
                    push!(detailed_results, (
                        method       = method_name,
                        tr_ratio     = tr,
                        n_subjects   = n_subj,
                        sim_id       = i,
                        auc_gmr      = res.auc_gmr,
                        auc_lo       = res.auc_lo,
                        auc_hi       = res.auc_hi,
                        auc_pass     = res.auc_pass,
                        cmax_gmr     = res.cmax_gmr,
                        cmax_lo      = res.cmax_lo,
                        cmax_hi      = res.cmax_hi,
                        cmax_pass    = res.cmax_pass,
                        overall_pass = res.overall_pass
                    ))
                end
            catch
                n_error += 1
                # silently count errors
            end
        end

        n_valid = n_sims - n_error
        rate           = n_valid > 0 ? (n_pass / n_valid) * 100 : NaN
        rate_unscaled  = n_valid > 0 ? (n_pass_unscaled / n_valid) * 100 : NaN

        push!(summary_results, (
            method              = method_name,
            tr_ratio            = tr,
            n_subjects          = n_subj,
            n_pass              = n_pass,
            n_pass_unscaled     = n_pass_unscaled,
            n_valid             = n_valid,
            n_error             = n_error,
            pass_rate           = rate,
            pass_rate_unscaled  = rate_unscaled
        ))

        # progress logged silently
    end

    return (summary = summary_results, detailed = detailed_results)
end
```

# Within-Reference %CV for Olanzapine (Partial Replicate)

Within-reference (intra-subject) variability estimated from the paired Reference
periods across 100 simulated partial replicate trials (60 subjects, T/R = 1.0).
This CV_WR determines whether RSABE (scaled limits) or standard TOST is applied.

```{julia}
#| output: false
cv_estimates = estimate_cv_within_ref(fixed_param_samples; n_subjects = 60, n_reps = 100)
nothing
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
println("AUC  within-reference %CV_WR = $(round(cv_estimates.auc_cv, digits=1))%")
println("Cmax within-reference %CV_WR = $(round(cv_estimates.cmax_cv, digits=1))%")
if cv_estimates.auc_cv > 30 || cv_estimates.cmax_cv > 30
    println("\nCV_WR > 30% detected → RSABE (scaled limits) applies for the high-variability metric(s).")
else
    println("\nCV_WR ≤ 30% for both metrics → standard unscaled TOST (80–125%) applies.")
end
```

# Visualization: Pass Rate by T/R Ratio and Sample Size
```{julia}
#| label: fig-passrate-lines
#| fig-cap: "Partial replicate BE pass rate (RSABE) across T/R ratios and sample sizes for each uncertainty method."
fig1 = Figure(size = (1400, 900))
methods_list = ["Fixed", "VCOV", "Bootstrap", "SIR"]
size_colors  = [:indigo, :dodgerblue, :steelblue, :seagreen, :orange, :crimson, :darkred]

for (idx, m) in enumerate(methods_list)
    row = (idx - 1) ÷ 2 + 1
    col = (idx - 1) % 2 + 1
    ax = Axis(fig1[row, col];
        xlabel = "T/R Ratio",
        ylabel = "BE Pass Rate (%)",
        title  = "$m Method (Partial Replicate, RSABE)",
        xticks = TR_RATIOS,
        yticks = 0:10:100
    )

    sub = filter(r -> r.method == m, all_summary)
    for (j, n) in enumerate(SAMPLE_SIZES)
        sub_n = sort(filter(r -> r.n_subjects == n, sub), :tr_ratio)
        scatterlines!(ax, sub_n.tr_ratio, sub_n.pass_rate;
            label     = "n=$n",
            color     = size_colors[j],
            marker    = :circle,
            markersize = 8,
            linewidth = 2
        )
    end

    hlines!(ax, [5.0]; color = :red, linestyle = :dash, linewidth = 1, label = "5% α")
    vlines!(ax, [0.80, 1.25]; color = :gray70, linestyle = :dot, linewidth = 1)

    if idx == 2
        axislegend(ax; position = :rt, labelsize = 9)
    end
end

supertitle = Label(fig1[0, :], "Partial Replicate BE Pass Rate (RSABE) by T/R Ratio and Sample Size"; fontsize = 20)
fig1
```

# Visualization: Pass Rate Heatmaps
```{julia}
#| label: fig-heatmaps
#| fig-cap: "Heatmap of partial replicate BE pass rates (RSABE) by sample size and T/R ratio."
fig2 = Figure(size = (1400, 900))

for (idx, m) in enumerate(methods_list)
    row = (idx - 1) ÷ 2 + 1
    col = (idx - 1) % 2 + 1

    sub = filter(r -> r.method == m, all_summary)
    mat = zeros(length(SAMPLE_SIZES), length(TR_RATIOS))
    for (i, n) in enumerate(SAMPLE_SIZES), (j, tr) in enumerate(TR_RATIOS)
        r = filter(r -> r.n_subjects == n && r.tr_ratio == tr, sub)
        mat[i, j] = nrow(r) > 0 ? r.pass_rate[1] : NaN
    end

    ax = Axis(fig2[row, col];
        xlabel = "T/R Ratio",
        ylabel = "Subjects (Partial Replicate)",
        title  = "$m Method (RSABE)",
        xticks = (1:length(TR_RATIOS), string.(TR_RATIOS)),
        yticks = (1:length(SAMPLE_SIZES), string.(SAMPLE_SIZES))
    )

    hm = heatmap!(ax, 1:length(TR_RATIOS), 1:length(SAMPLE_SIZES), mat';
        colormap = :RdYlGn, colorrange = (0, 100)
    )

    for (i, n) in enumerate(SAMPLE_SIZES), (j, tr) in enumerate(TR_RATIOS)
        txt = isnan(mat[i, j]) ? "—" : "$(round(Int, mat[i, j]))%"
        text!(ax, j, i; text = txt, align = (:center, :center),
            fontsize = 11, color = mat[i, j] > 50 ? :black : :white)
    end

    if idx == 2
        Colorbar(fig2[row, col + 1], hm; label = "Pass Rate (%)")
    end
end

supertitle2 = Label(fig2[0, :], "Partial Replicate BE Pass Rate Heatmap (RSABE): Sample Size vs T/R Ratio"; fontsize = 20)
fig2
```

# Visualization: 90% CI Bounds (LB and UB) for AUC
```{julia}
#| label: fig-ci-bounds
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of AUC 90% CI lower and upper bounds (Fixed, n=30, Partial Replicate)."
fig6 = Figure(size = (1400, 800))

for (j, tr) in enumerate(TR_RATIOS)
    sub_tr = filter(r -> r.tr_ratio == tr, detail_sub)
    nrow(sub_tr) == 0 && continue

    # Lower Bound
    ax_lb = Axis(fig6[1, j];
        xlabel = j == 3 ? "AUC 90% CI Lower Bound" : "",
        ylabel = j == 1 ? "Count" : "",
        title  = "T/R = $tr"
    )
    hist!(ax_lb, sub_tr.auc_lo; bins = 25, color = (:coral, 0.7), strokecolor = :black, strokewidth = 0.5)
    vlines!(ax_lb, [0.80]; color = :red, linestyle = :dash, linewidth = 2, label = "BE limit")

    # Upper Bound
    ax_ub = Axis(fig6[2, j];
        xlabel = j == 3 ? "AUC 90% CI Upper Bound" : "",
        ylabel = j == 1 ? "Count" : ""
    )
    hist!(ax_ub, sub_tr.auc_hi; bins = 25, color = (:mediumpurple, 0.7), strokecolor = :black, strokewidth = 0.5)
    vlines!(ax_ub, [1.25]; color = :red, linestyle = :dash, linewidth = 2, label = "BE limit")
end
```

# Visualization: Effect of Sample Size on CI Width
```{julia}
#| label: fig-ci-width
#| fig-cap: "Median AUC GMR and 90% CI bounds narrowing with increasing sample size (Partial Replicate)."
fig7 = Figure(size = (1000, 600))

# Calculate median CI width (AUC) by sample size at T/R = 1.0
detail_tr1 = filter(r -> r.method == "Fixed" && r.tr_ratio == 1.0, all_detailed)

ci_width_summary = combine(
    groupby(detail_tr1, :n_subjects),
    :auc_lo  => median => :median_lb,
    :auc_hi  => median => :median_ub,
    :auc_gmr => median => :median_gmr,
    [:auc_hi, :auc_lo] => ((hi, lo) -> median(hi .- lo)) => :median_ci_width
)
sort!(ci_width_summary, :n_subjects)

ax7 = Axis(fig7[1, 1];
    xlabel = "Subjects (Partial Replicate)",
    ylabel = "Value",
    title  = "AUC: Median GMR and 90% CI Bounds vs Sample Size (T/R = 1.0, Fixed, Partial Replicate)",
    xticks = SAMPLE_SIZES
)

band!(ax7, ci_width_summary.n_subjects,
    ci_width_summary.median_lb, ci_width_summary.median_ub;
    color = (:steelblue, 0.3), label = "Median 90% CI")
scatterlines!(ax7, ci_width_summary.n_subjects, ci_width_summary.median_gmr;
    color = :steelblue, marker = :circle, markersize = 10, linewidth = 2, label = "Median GMR")
scatterlines!(ax7, ci_width_summary.n_subjects, ci_width_summary.median_lb;
    color = :coral, marker = :dtriangle, markersize = 8, linewidth = 1.5, linestyle = :dash, label = "Median LB")
scatterlines!(ax7, ci_width_summary.n_subjects, ci_width_summary.median_ub;
    color = :mediumpurple, marker = :utriangle, markersize = 8, linewidth = 1.5, linestyle = :dash, label = "Median UB")
hlines!(ax7, [0.80, 1.25]; color = :red, linestyle = :dot, linewidth = 1, label = "BE limits")

axislegend(ax7; position = :rt, labelsize = 10)
fig7
```
